name: Mansi
catalog_quote: Main stress is initial; secondary stress on subsequent odd-numbered syllables. Sources differ on whether or not final syllables are stressed. (Hayes 1995:200)

audit.recode_to: Keep primary = fixed initial (classification fixed-strict, dom true), but change the rhythmic rule from alternating stress from the left to stress placement coded per word length as 10 100 1010 10100 101010 1010100 10101010 (1 = a stressed syllable) (secondary stress on odd non-final syllables), citing Riese & Bradley 2020:26 verbatim (held) as quote/cite/loc, with StressTyp2/Hayes 1995:200 demoted to refs; add a caution that Normanskaja 2020 (LU 56:133-146, instrumental) reports lexically variable verb stress in Ob and Khulimsunt-Sosva speech while conceding literary Sosva is root-stressed.
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: The record has no deciding quotation of its own; its classification is the StressTyp2 profile, whose only banked text (Hayes 1995:200, confirmed verbatim in the held StressTyp2 SQL dump) explicitly says sources differ on final-syllable stress, and whose own ST1 remark says degenerate (final monosyllabic) feet are not allowed by the descriptive source consulted — so the database is internally inconsistent with the 10|101|10101 profile it coded. The one specialist description we hold, Riese & Bradley 2020 p.26 (Riese is the author of the 2001 LINCOM grammar), states secondary stress on odd syllables 'mit Ausnahme der letzten Silbe', which yields 10|100|1010|10100. Pokrovskaya 2022:47 (downloaded) confirms initial primary + odd-syllable secondaries citing Riese 2001:17 and is silent on finals; Pajusalu et al. 2018:192 (downloaded) adds an unsourced weight-sensitivity flag; Normanskaja 2020 (downloaded, Praat-based
audit.second_reader_evidence: Quote finding confirmed: record has empty quote/cite/loc; coding rests on the StressTyp2 entry= Hayes 1995:200, verbatim at line 29126 ('..Sources differ on whether or not final syllables are stressed'); passages 1382-1384 (Kálmán, Lakó, Rombandeeva) are NULL; ST1 remark row 1590 (line 15541) 'Degenerate feet are not allowed according to the descriptive source that we have consulted'. sources.quote: 'In the northern dialects of Mansi word stress is fixed on the first syllable; subsequent odd syllables may receive secondary stress, even syllables remain unstressed (Riese 2001: 17)'; adds from her own field phonetics that duration is the primary cue of word stress and phonologically long vowels are absent from even syllables. Silent on the final-syllable question.

sources.citation: Normanskaja, Julia. 2020. The system of variable stress in Northern Mansi dialects and its external correspondences. Linguistica Uralica 56(2): 133-146. DOI 10.3176/lu.2020.2.05 (open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Praat-based field study (Ob dialect 2013, Sosva at Khulimsunt 2016) claiming three verbal accent paradigms (stress fixed on root / fixed off the root / alternating 1st~2nd syllable), e.g. Sosva teˈɣəm 'I eat' vs xujeˈɣəm 'I lie'; concedes 'in literary Sosva stress is fixed on the root of the word' and that Steinitz 1955:331-336 has Sosva accent 'usually on the first syllable'. Minority (Moscow accentological school) position.
